title: Improve the Surzion storefront's DATA MODEL, BUSINESS LOGIC and ACCESS so it wor
description: Improve the Surzion storefront's DATA MODEL, BUSINESS LOGIC and ACCESS so it wor
originating_prompt:
Improve the Surzion storefront's DATA MODEL, BUSINESS LOGIC and ACCESS so it works like a standard e-commerce shop. Do NOT change any smart pages in this turn (pages come in a later turn). Do not ask clarifying questions — make sensible choices and list them at the end. Customers and partners sign in as this application's PROJECT USERS (application.auth providers "project-users", self-registration gives role "customer") — keep that; never add password/login columns to any table.

1. Customer accounts and orders
   - surz_order: add row security so a signed-in shopper only ever sees and changes their OWN orders: rule column REGISTRY_ID, source user_id (exempt roles admin, func-admin). Keep REGISTRY_ID as the payment owner column.
   - When an order is saved, capture the customer automatically: a pre_commit on surz_order that finds the customer master (surz_customer) by REGISTRY_ID (else by EMAIL, else by PHONE — shoppers may identify with a mobile number only), creates it if missing (name, email, phone, ship address from the order) or updates the changed contact details, and sets the order's CUSTOMER_ID before the mandatory check — so CUSTOMER_ID is never something the shopper must type. Also save the order's delivery address into the customer's address book (see 2) if it is not already there.
   - The online payment action on surz_order must declare `cod_status_value: "COD"` in its payment block so Cash on Delivery works (paid_values already includes COD).

2. Address book — a NEW master transaction `surz_customer_address`: many delivery addresses per customer. Columns: ADDRESS_ID (auto), REGISTRY_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, LABEL (e.g. Home / Clinic / Hospital), CONTACT_NAME, PHONE, ADDRESS_LINE1, ADDRESS_LINE2, CITY, STATE_NAME, PINCODE, IS_DEFAULT (Y/N). Row-secured by REGISTRY_ID source user_id (exempt admin, func-admin). Only one default per customer (validation or pre_commit).

3. Saved payment preferences — a NEW master `surz_customer_payment_method`: many per customer. Columns: METHOD_ID (auto), REGISTRY_ID, CUSTOMER_ID, METHOD_TYPE (COD / UPI / CARD / NETBANKING), LABEL, UPI_ID (optional), CARD_BRAND + CARD_LAST4 (display only), GATEWAY_TOKEN (the gateway's saved-instrument token only), IS_DEFAULT. NEVER store a full card number, CVV or expiry. Row-secured by REGISTRY_ID like the address book.

4. Product reviews — a NEW transaction `surz_product_review`: REVIEW_ID (auto), PRODUCT_CODE (must exist in the product master), RATING (1-5, mandatory), TITLE, REVIEW_TEXT (mandatory), REVIEWER_NAME, REVIEWER_REGISTRY_ID, STATUS (PENDING / APPROVED / REJECTED, default PENDING, protected from shoppers), MODERATOR_NOTE, plus audit columns. NOT row-secured (approved reviews are public). Add Approve and Reject action buttons (set STATUS; Reject asks for a MODERATOR_NOTE). Add it to the navigation in an admin area so the functional admin (func-admin) can see ALL reviews and decide which are shown; customers get no direct grant on it (reviews are submitted through the storefront's review block, which writes them server-side as PENDING).

5. Partners — add a functional role `partner` (Access). When a partner application (surz_partner / surz_partner_apply, whichever holds the approval) is APPROVED, grant the applicant's registry account the `partner` role using the Python business-logic runtime API `api.grant_role(<REGISTRY_ID>, "partner")` (and `api.revoke_role` if a partner is deactivated/rejected). Give `partner` the grants the partner portal objects need (list/load on surz_partner and surz_partner_order, plus what the customer role already has).

6. Access grants: customer role — list/load/add/save on surz_order (row security keeps it to their own; the storefront checkout needs `add`, My orders needs `list`), list/load/add/edit/save/delete on surz_customer_address and surz_customer_payment_method; NO grant on surz_product_review (reviews are written server-side by the reviews block); STATUS on surz_product_review is protected (protect: 1) so only the Approve/Reject actions change it; func-admin sees everything.

7. Wishlist is client-side in the browser (no table needed). Make sure the product sku used by add_to_cart on the site equals PRODUCT_CODE (the order line's key, which must exist in the product master) — note any page where it doesn't so the next turn fixes it.

Create the tables (Database_Design + deploy), generate/finish all business logic, and run the business-logic review. Finally verify the models (finalize + verify) and summarise every change.
result_summary:
tions:** `bl_schema_verify.py` reported "no body" for every `.py` file. The runner judged that a SQL-only check, so none of the functions was confirmed by that tool.
- **`api.grant_role` / `api.revoke_role` on partner approve/reject:** never run.
- **Business-logic review:** the coder reviewed the code by reading it. It could not run the review tools, so no tool-based review was done.
- **"Finalize + verify":** I had no such command, so unit tests were the only verification.
- **Test rows:** the unit tests left sample rows in the live preview data, including a test review RV-00001. I did not remove them.

**What changed**
- **`surz_order`:**
  - It is now row-secured by REGISTRY_ID (exempt admin and func-admin), and the Pay now button has `cod_status_value: "COD"`.
  - CUSTOMER_ID is now optional and hidden. A new first `pre_commit`, `surz_capture_customer`, finds the customer by registry id, then email, then phone. It creates or updates the customer, sets CUSTOMER_ID, and adds the delivery address to the address book if missing.
- **New `surz_customer_address`:** columns as specified, row-secured, with a `pre_commit` that keeps one default address per customer.
- **New `surz_customer_payment_method`:** columns as specified, row-secured. There are no card number, CVV or expiry columns. CARD_LAST4 must be four digits, and GATEWAY_TOKEN is hidden and set to NULL on add. It has a one-default-per-customer rule.
- **New `surz_product_review`:** not row-secured, with the columns you listed. STATUS defaults to PENDING and is protected. Approve and Reject buttons set STATUS, and Reject requires a MODERATOR_NOTE. It is in a Moderation folder visible only to admin and func-admin.
- **Partner role:** approving a partner in `surz_partner` calls `api.grant_role(registry_id, "partner")`, and rejecting calls `api.revoke_role`. `surz_partner_apply` has no approve or reject, so I left it alone.
- **Access (`application.json`):**
  - customer: list/load/add/save on `surz_order`, and list/load/add/edit/save/delete on the address book and payment methods.
  - partner: everything customer has, plus list/load on `surz_partner` and `surz_partner_order`.
  - admin and func-admin: all actions on the new objects and on `surz_order`.
  - Reviews: no customer grant.
- **Navigation:** the address book and payment methods are under the Sales folder.
- **Files touched:**
  - Models: `model_surz_order.json`, `model_surz_customer.json`, `model_surz_partner.json` (spec notes only), and the three new `model_surz_*.json`.
  - Database_Design: `SURZ_ORDER.json`, `SURZ_CUSTOMER.json`, and three new `SURZ_*.json`.
  - Code: five new files under `src/transaction_models/`, plus edits to `surz_partner/action__surz_partner_approve.py` and `action__surz_partner_reject.py`.
  - `application.json`.
- **FRS:** the project has no `requirement_doc.md`, so none was updated.

**Choices I made**
- `SURZ_CUSTOMER.EMAIL` is no longer mandatory (model and database design), so phone-only shoppers get a NULL email instead of a fake one.
- CUSTOMER_ID is hidden on the order form, so admins can't pick a customer there. Set `hidden: 0` if you want that.
- The `partner` role is granted through the grant list, since I didn't find a separate functional-role declaration.
- Reject on an already-rejected review and Approve on an already-approved one are hidden by `visible_when`.

**For the next turn (pages)**
- **SKU mismatch:** all 24 smart pages with `add_to_cart` use slug SKUs such as `artery-forceps-crile`, `allison-lung-retractor` and `adson-brown-tissue-forceps`. PRODUCT_CODE values look like `SURZ-0015`, so they don't match. The pages need to send PRODUCT_CODE as the sku.
- **Reviews block:** it must write PENDING reviews server-side, since customers have no grant on reviews.
- **Partner registry id:** the `partner` role is only granted when the applicant's REGISTRY_ID is known at approval. Nothing retries it later, so a partner approved before they have an account won't get the role.
